examples.question_text:
The table shows the number of pets in each household surveyed.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Pets }x&\text{Frequency }f\\\hline0&0\\1&3\\3&6\\5&7\\7&2\\9&0\end{array}$
a. How many households were surveyed, and how many pets did they have altogether?
b. Find the range.
c. Find the mode.
d. Find the median.
e. Find the mean, correct to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Build the $fx$ and cumulative frequency columns.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&f&fx&\text{c.f.}\\\hline0&0&0&0\\1&3&3&3\\3&6&18&9\\5&7&35&16\\7&2&14&18\\9&0&0&18\end{array}$
a. $\Sigma f=18$ and $\Sigma fx=70$. There are $18$ households and $70$ pets.
b. Ignore values with frequency $0$.
$\text{Range}=7-1=6$
c. The greatest frequency is $7$, at $x=5$.
$\text{Mode}=5$
d. There are $18$ values. The $9$th score is $3$ and the $10$th is $5$.
$\text{Median}=\frac{3+5}{2}=4$
e. $\overline{x}=\frac{70}{18}=3.8888\ldots\approx3.9$ pets per household.

examples.question_text:
The cumulative frequency table shows the number of pets in each household.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Pets }x&\text{c.f.}\\\hline0&4\\1&11\\2&20\\3&25\\4&28\end{array}$
a. Find the frequency of each value.
b. Find the mean number of pets per household, correct to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
a. Subtract each cumulative frequency from the next. The first frequency is $4$.
$11-4=7$, $20-11=9$, $25-20=5$, $28-25=3$.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c}x&f&fx\\\hline0&4&0\\1&7&7\\2&9&18\\3&5&15\\4&3&12\end{array}$
b. $\Sigma f=28$ and $\Sigma fx=52$.
The households with $0$ pets still count in the total frequency.
$\overline{x}=\frac{52}{28}=1.8571\ldots\approx1.9$ pets per household.

examples.question_text:
Find the mode for each frequency table.
a. $\begin{array}{c|c}x&f\\\hline1&4\\3&4\\5&4\end{array}$
b. $\begin{array}{c|c}x&f\\\hline1&3\\2&5\\6&5\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
a. Each value has the same frequency, so there is no mode.
b. The greatest frequency is $5$, at both $x=2$ and $x=6$.
The modes are $2$ and $6$, not the frequency $5$.

Read each column height as a frequency. No student has $5$ siblings.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&f&fx&\text{c.f.}\\\hline0&3&0&3\\1&6&6&9\\2&4&8&13\\3&6&18&19\\4&2&8&21\\5&0&0&21\end{array}$
The smallest observed value is $0$ and the largest is $4$.
$\text{Range}=4-0=4$
The tallest columns both have frequency $6$, at $x=1$ and $x=3$. The modes are $1$ and $3$ siblings.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Position}&=\frac{21+1}{2}\\&=11\end{aligned}$
Scores $10$ to $13$ are all $2$, so the median is $2$ siblings.
$\Sigma f=21$ and $\Sigma fx=40$.
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}&=\frac{40}{21}\\&\approx1.9\end{aligned}$
The mean is $1.9$ siblings per student.

Count the dots above each value to build the frequency table.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&f&fx&\text{c.f.}\\\hline0&2&0&2\\1&3&3&5\\2&5&10&10\\3&3&9&13\\4&2&8&15\end{array}$
$\Sigma f=15$ and $\Sigma fx=30$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Position}&=\frac{15+1}{2}\\&=8\end{aligned}$
Scores $6$ to $10$ are all $2$, so the median is $2$ books.
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}&=\frac{30}{15}\\&=2\end{aligned}$
The mean is $2$ books per student.

The first frequency is $3$. Subtract consecutive cumulative frequencies for the remaining values.
$8-3=5$, $10-8=2$, $17-10=7$, $20-17=3$.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&\text{c.f.}&f&fx\\\hline0&3&3&0\\1&8&5&5\\2&10&2&4\\3&17&7&21\\4&20&3&12\end{array}$
$\Sigma f=20$ and $\Sigma fx=42$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Position}&=\frac{20+1}{2}\\&=10.5\end{aligned}$
The $10$th score is $2$ and the $11$th score is $3$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Median}&=\frac{2+3}{2}\\&=2.5\end{aligned}$
The median is $2.5$ books.
$\begin{aligned}\overline{x}&=\frac{42}{20}\\&=2.1\end{aligned}$
The mean is $2.1$ books per student.

coverage.summary: Retained all four existing examples, preserving three exactly and improving the ogive example's diagram formatting and solution annotations. Added three examples covering ordinary histograms, dot plots and cumulative histograms, with different source values and no additional assessed methods. All 33 assessment locators are mapped by method only; practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. Final-size diagram capture and independent review of the new examples remain later coordinator stages.

examples.derivation: Cumulative frequencies 3, 7, 14, 18, 23 give 23 observations. Half the total is 11.5. The ogive crossing has horizontal coordinate 2.5+(11.5-7)/(14-7)=3.142857, matching the solution guide inside the 3-books column. The 12th observation is 3 books, so the median is 3. The revised diagram preserves the original data and method.

Histogram frequencies for values 0–5 are 3, 6, 4, 6, 2, 0. Their sum is 21; weighted products are 0, 6, 8, 18, 8, 0, totalling 40. Cumulative frequencies are 3, 9, 13, 19, 21, 21. Observed endpoints give range 4. Frequencies 6 give modes 1 and 3. Position (21+1)/2=11 lies at value 2. Mean 40/21=1.904761… rounds to 1.9.

Counting plotted dots gives frequencies 2, 3, 5, 3, 2 for values 0–4. There are 15 observations and weighted total 0+3+10+9+8=30. Cumulative frequencies are 2, 5, 10, 13, 15. Position (15+1)/2=8 lies at value 2, giving median 2 books. Mean 30/15=2 books.

Cumulative histogram heights 3, 8, 10, 17, 20 yield frequencies 3, 5, 2, 7, 3 for values 0–4. Weighted products 0, 5, 4, 21, 12 total 42. Of 20 observations, the 10th is 2 and the 11th is 3, so median (2+3)/2=2.5 books. Mean 42/20=2.1 books.
